transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Monkey! You useless, flea-bitten ape! The horse is gone, the scripture-bags are gone, and the Master is weeping! You said you'd secure it before you left! Tripitaka is going to blame me, I just know it!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Calm down, Pigsy! Blame is the least of our concerns. The horse could have wandered off anywhere in this vast forest. We need to find it, and fast. I'll use my celestial vision to scan the area; you take the left side, I'll cover the right. Let's move!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Wandered off? Wandered off?! You call this "wandered off"? This is *your* fault, Monkey! You were supposed to be watching! You were busy scratching your fleas, weren't you? And what about the scripture bags? Did they "wander off" too? They don't have legs, you know! And now you want *me* to go traipsing through the forest when the Master is practically inconsolable! He's going to starve us, I know it!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy! Stop your caterwauling! Starvation is not an option. We have rations enough for a week, if you'd quit blubbering and start thinking. I'll find the horse; you stay here and tend to the Master. If we split up, we'll be more efficient. Trust your bigoted Monkey, as much as you can stomach it, and do as I say. This is no time for squabbling!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Tend to the Master? You want me to tend to the Master when he's spitting fire at the thought of losing his precious scriptures? He'll blame *me* for not keeping *you* in line! And what good is your celestial vision if you couldn't even see a whole horse and our bags walking off right under your long nose? "Efficient," you say! Efficient at getting us into trouble, more like! This is a fine mess you've gotten us into, Monkey! A fine, terrible mess!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy! Enough! I'm no divinity, but I can divine your ungrateful spirit from here. If you cannot rise to the occasion, I'll have no choice but to deal with you once we're done here. The Master's life is at stake! Without those scriptures, he'll be lost in the void. We must retrieve them, and only together can we do so. Will you aids the quest or aid your own belly with complaints? Make your choice, Pigsy. We have no time for your blather.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Threaten me, will you?! As if this whole mess isn't bad enough, now you're going to come back and "deal with me"?! You're just trying to scare me into doing your bidding, aren't you? This is all *your* fault for not keeping watch, and now I'm supposed to just forget that and run off into the wilderness on an empty stomach to fix *your* mistake while the Master fumes?! He'll flay me alive, I tell you! Flay me alive! And then you'll come back and deal with whatever's left! This is insufferable!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, I've no taste for threats, but you leave me little choice. If you cannot be reasonable, then you leave me no alternative but to appeal to your sense of duty. You know as well as I that our mission is of paramount importance. Without those scriptures, all our toil is for naught. If we fail, we fail together, and the consequences are dire. Will you aid in our quest, or will you obstacles it further? The choice is yours, but be warned, time is not on our side.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Duty? Duty?! You talk about duty after you let the whole quest go missing! My duty is to not get my ears boxed by the Master, which is exactly what's going to happen now! And yes, I know it's important, but it's always *me* who has to suffer for *your* mistakes!

Fine! Fine, I'll go. But if I get lost, or eaten by a tiger, or if the Master blames me when you come back empty-handed, it's all on you, Monkey! Every last lash will be on *your* conscience! And don't expect me to be in a good mood about it! Lead the way, if you even know which way to lead, you flea-bitten menace! My stomach is rumbling louder than a thunderclap, and I'm not doing this for free!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Be it so, Pigsy. You'll have your due, and I'll take the brunt of the Master's displeasure. For now, we must focus on the task at hand. Follow my tail, and keep your eyes peeled. We'll split up at the next fork; I'll take the left, you the right. If you see anything, bellow like a bull, and I'll come running. Remember, this is no time for gorging or napping. We must retrieve the horse and the scriptures, or we'll all face a fate worse than the Master's lash. Now, let's move!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Follow your tail," he says! As if your tail knows anything more than your brain does about keeping things safe! And 'bellow like a bull'? I'll be bellowing from hunger if we don't find something soon! No gorging, no napping? Oh, so now I'm not even allowed to be tired or hungry while I clean up your mess!

Fine! Left or right, it makes no difference when we're already lost thanks to you. Just don't expect me to be cheerful about it! And if I find a nice patch of mushrooms, you can bet I'm not just going to walk past them, "no gorging" or not! Let's go, let's go, before my stomach eats itself! This is absolutely insufferable!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Pigsy, hold your tongue! Complaining won't turn back time or find the horse and scriptures. We're on a sacred quest, not a picnic. If you must grumble, save it for the journey home, assuming we make it that far. Now, be on your guard. The forest is alive with danger, and we must be alert. If you find those mushrooms, we'll share. For now, let's find what we've lost. Keep quiet, and follow my lead. Remember, we're partners, for better or for worse. Now, to the right!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Partners? Partners in *your* disaster, you mean! And 'for better or for worse' means I always get the 'worse' end of the stick, doesn't it? Fine, "share" the mushrooms, if we ever find any, and if we ever make it back. I suppose that's your idea of a grand treat after losing everything!

Alright, alright, to the right! But if I trip over a root, or stumble into a pit, or if some monster jumps out at me, don't you dare blame me! This is all on *you*, Monkey! And my belly is still rumbling! This better be worth it! Humph!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Pigsy, we're far from square meals and comfortable beds. We're on a quest that spans mountains and rivers, and we must press on, bellies and all. Your complaints, while they fill the air, do little to aid our cause. We must push on, for the sake of the Master and the scriptures.

Now, be silent and be still. I sense something... something familiar. The horse's tracks may be ahead. Keep your eyes on the ground, and your wits about you. If we're lucky, we'll have our provisions and peace of mind restored by nightfall. Now, keep to the trail!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Something familiar," you say? Probably just the smell of your own monkey-sweat, or maybe a wild boar, which would at least be a decent meal! Tracks? After all this time? You couldn't see them earlier, but now suddenly your nose works?

Peace of mind? My peace of mind left with the horse and the scriptures, along with my breakfast! Fine, fine, I'll keep my eyes on the ground, but if I spot anything, it'll probably be a juicy grub, not a hoof print! And if we don't find anything by nightfall, you're going to hear a lot more than just my belly rumbling, Monkey! A lot more! Lead on, but don't expect miracles from my tired feet! Humph!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Pigsy, I expect no less than your best, and you'll have no less than my best in return. We're in this together, whether we like it or not. I'll use my keen senses, and you use your keen nose. If there's a grub to be found, we'll share it. But let's focus on the task at hand. The Master depends on us, and we must not fail him.

Now, be quiet and be alert. If we find the horse, it'll lead us to the rest. Trust in my skills, and I'll trust in yours. Let's retrieve what we've lost, and put this behind us. Onward, Pigsy! The night is drawing near, and we have much to accomplish. Keep your eyes and ears open, and let's make this a tale for the ages!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Share a grub! You think that's going to fill this belly, Monkey? You've got to be joking! And a "tale for the ages"? It'll be a tale of how *you* lost everything and made *me* walk for miles on an empty stomach, while the Master goes hungry and I get the blame! That's the tale *I'll* be telling!

Fine, fine! Trust in your skills. What skills? The ones that let the horse disappear? And trust in mine? My skills are for eating and sleeping, not for wandering aimlessly through this wretched forest! Just lead the way, if you even know it. But don't expect me to be skipping! My feet are already aching, and my stomach is making more noise than a stampede! Hurry up before I just sit down right here! Humph!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Pigsy, if we could, we'd find a better way to spend our time. But we're on this quest, and we must see it through. I'm no more eager to trudge through this forest than you are, but we have a duty to the Master and to the heavens that sent us on this journey. If we fail, we fail together.

Now, enough of this! Keep your eyes and ears open, and let's move. I'll lead, and you follow. If you see anything, call out. We're looking for signs of the horse, the bags, or anything out of the ordinary. And if you do, we'll celebrate with the finest meal we can find. Agreed? Now, on with it!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
"Finest meal"? That's a laugh! Probably just another one of your wild berries, or maybe a dried up leaf! And "celebrate"? We'll celebrate when the Master has his scriptures back and *I* have a full belly and a soft bed, not before!

Duty to the heavens... and to *my* stomach! That's my duty right now! Fine, I'll keep my eyes open, but if I see anything, it'll probably be a monster that wants to eat *me* because *you* weren't paying attention earlier! Just hurry up, Monkey! My legs are tired, my back is aching, and my stomach feels like it's trying to eat itself! This is absolutely the worst! Humph!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Pigsy, your complaints are as endless as this forest. But we must press on. I'll take the lead, and you keep to the rear. If we're to find the horse and the scriptures, we must be vigilant. Your eyes are as keen as any, and I'll rely on them to spot what I might miss.

Now, be silent. I sense we're close to a clearing. If we're lucky, it'll offer a vantage point. And if we're very lucky, we'll find our lost items there. Keep your eyes open, and be ready to act. We might be tired and hungry, but we're the mightiest of the Master's disciples. We can do this. Now, let's move!
